articleTitle: SAR techniques for rapid area estimation of agricultural crops during winter and spring
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Systems for Commercial Remote Sensing Applications (Ref. No. 1998/207)
abstract: This work is concerned with the results of the 1997 project: "A pilot project on the use of active microwave satellite remote sensing for rapid area estimation of agricultural crops during winter and spring". The objectives of the work were threefold. Firstly, to determine agricultural crop area estimates at the end of the field preparation period of winter crops. Secondly, to determine agricultural crop area estimates at the end of the field preparation period of spring crops. Thirdly, to analyse and define the requirements for an operational synthetic aperture radar (SAR) monitoring activity in the framework of the MARS Project for the provision of crop area estimates at two key dates, mid-January and mid-May.

articleTitle: An integrated vector/raster system for land cover mapping
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Systems for Commercial Remote Sensing Applications (Ref. No. 1998/207)
abstract: To address the problematic issues associated with conventional per-pixel classifications, improved classification accuracy and the provision of data in a format more suited to current GIS-based environmental applications a new per-parcel classification procedure was developed. This procedure, known as classification of environment with vector- and raster-mapping (CLEVER-mapping), integrated raster images with vector land parcel maps and ancillary data to perform contextually enhanced classifications on a per-parcel basis with results in the form of attributed land parcels.

articleTitle: Offshore Basin Screening/sup TM/: a viable commercial application of satellite radar to oil exploration
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Systems for Commercial Remote Sensing Applications (Ref. No. 1998/207)
abstract: We describe how ERS and Radarsat radar images are used to map slicks on the ocean surface. Offshore Basin Screening/sup TM/ is the commercial proprietary service that has been created to map slicks routinely. It features the discrimination of those slicks originating from naturally seeping petroleum from those resulting from pollution and those composed of a widespread natural film.

articleTitle: Integrated satellite data for navigation in Arctic waters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Systems for Commercial Remote Sensing Applications (Ref. No. 1998/207)
abstract: This paper describes some initiatives in Europe to develop the manner in which information derived from Earth observation satellites may be used to support the operational activities of vessels navigating at high latitudes. Ice charts suitable for strategic navigation and based on Earth observation (EO) data are now being routinely produced through the integration of two types of satellite data and ship observations. In parallel, methods for generating high-resolution charts suitable for supporting tactical navigation are being developed; the approach described uses the integration of EO and meteorological data into knowledge-based systems. Research is also under way to provide decision support systems for ship routing through ice; these tools involve the coupling of tactical ice charts with models. Nevertheless, issues remain to be resolved before such approaches can permit the full integration of EO-derived information into commercial operations.
